---

## Why the originals were fabricated

Each original entry showed the classic LLM-hallucination signature:
- Real, prestigious venue (IEEE Access / IEEE TSE / IEEE TDSC) paired with a plausible-but-nonexistent title.
- Generic author initials.
- Placeholder page ranges: `12345-12356`, `1-20`, `2345-2358`.
- Generic bibkeys `b1`/`b2`/`b3` (vs. the descriptive keys used by all real entries, e.g. `malul2024`, `borg`, `auer2002`).

Verification method: queried Crossref by title/author for each entry. None of the three returned a matching record. The closest real items were unrelated papers by different authors in different venues.

**Removed (fabricated):**
```
\bibitem{b1} G. E. O. Kremer, "Kubernetes Security: A Comprehensive Review," \emph{IEEE Access}, vol. 9, pp. 12345-12356, 2021.
```

**Added (verified):**
```
\bibitem{b1}
M. S. Islam Shamim, F. A. Bhuiyan, and A. Rahman, "XI Commandments of Kubernetes Security: A Systematization of Knowledge Related to Kubernetes Security Practices," in \emph{Proc. 2020 IEEE Secure Development Conf. (SecDev)}, 2020, pp. 58--64, doi: 10.1109/SecDev45635.2020.00025.
```

**Verification:** Crossref DOI `10.1109/secdev45635.2020.00025` — confirmed title, authors (Md. Shazibul Islam Shamim, Farzana Ahamed Bhuiyan, Akond Rahman), venue (2020 IEEE SecDev), pages 58-64.
**Topical fit:** Supports the intro claim that Kubernetes "remains prone to security misconfigurations." A peer-reviewed systematization of Kubernetes security practices is a stronger, on-topic source than the generic review it replaces.

## In-text citation (unchanged prose, line ~185)

The single sentence that cites all three keys was left as-is, because the replacement sources fit the existing claims:

> "Kubernetes has become the de facto operating system for the cloud, yet its declarative configuration model remains prone to security misconfigurations `\cite{shamim2020}`, `\cite{shu2017}`. ... - `\cite{shamim2020}` (K8s security SoK) + `\cite{shu2017}` (Docker Hub vulnerabilities) → "prone to security misconfigurations" ✓
- `\cite{xia2023}` (APR with LLMs) → "potential for automated repair" ✓

## Change 4 — `\bibitem{aardvark}` URL hardening (not a fabrication)

The `aardvark` entry was real but cited only the OpenAI homepage, which both panel reviewers flagged as resembling the fabrication pattern.

**Before:**
```
\bibitem{aardvark}
OpenAI, "Aardvark: AI Security Agent (Beta)," 2025. [Online]. Available: \url{https://openai.com/}
```

**After:**
```
\bibitem{aardvark}
OpenAI, "Introducing Aardvark: OpenAI's agentic security researcher (Beta)," 2025. [Online]. Available: \url{https://openai.com/index/introducing-aardvark/}
```

**Verification:** The specific announcement page is real. `https://openai.com/index/introducing-aardvark/` returns HTTP 403 to automated clients (Cloudflare bot challenge, same as the pre-existing `swe_bench_verified` ref), but the Internet Archive has a status-200 snapshot dated 2026-05-27 (`web.archive.org/web/20260527002252/https://openai.com/index/introducing-aardvark/`), confirming the page exists. This is a URL-precision fix, not a fabrication removal.

A blind subagent bibliography audit found that the `kubeintellect` entry listed the wrong authors. The arXiv ID was correct, but the author field was a misattribution (same error class as a fabrication: wrong names attached to a real paper).

```
\bibitem{kubeintellect}
M. S. Ardebili and A. Bartolini, "KubeIntellect: A Modular LLM-Orchestrated Agent Framework for End-to-End Kubernetes Management," \emph{arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.02449}, 2025.
```

**Verification:** arXiv:2509.02449 abstract page `citation_author` metadata lists exactly two authors — Mohsen Seyedkazemi Ardebili and Andrea Bartolini (University of Bologna). No "Y. Li" appears in the author list. Title confirmed identical.

## Change 7 — Fix margin overflow (overfull \hbox) before final build

After installing a LaTeX toolchain and compiling, 7 overfull \hbox warnings were observed (worst ~30pt). Two source edits reduced these and, more importantly, eliminated all real margin overflow in the rendered PDF:

- Added `\usepackage{xurl}` (after `hyperref`) so long GitHub URLs/paths break across lines instead of running into the margin.
- Trimmed the fixed column in the comparison table (`tab:comparison`) from `p{2.5in}` to `p{2.2in}` (its overflow dropped 11.1pt -> 3.9pt).
- (No new `\emergencystretch` added; the source already set `\emergencystretch=3em`.)

**Verification (rendered-geometry, not just log):** A per-page scan of the compiled `access.pdf` text/block bounding boxes found ZERO pages with any text crossing the right margin (limit x=582pt on a 612pt-wide page). The 6 residual log-level overfull warnings are inside a `\resizebox` (measured pre-scaling) and do not overflow in the final output.

## Change 8 — Prose pass to remove AI-generated / product-manual style (R1 & R3)

Reviewer 1 ("seems generated partially by GenAI") and Reviewer 3 ("written in a style more like a product manual") reacted to the writing style, which earlier changes had not touched. This pass removes the specific stylistic tells without altering any technical claim, number, table, figure, or citation.

- **Neutralized rubric framing:** "Table~X fixes the COSMIC-style 'missing configuration' gap by listing every Grok/xAI knob..." -> "Table~X lists the Grok/xAI configuration (model, temperature, retries, timeout) used in these sweeps."

  1. "How we differ" -> "Distinguishing characteristics." (plain paragraph)
  2. "Quickstart: 3 commands" -> "Reproducing the results." (commands rendered as inline \texttt{} instead of a boxed command list)
  3. "Notation" box -> unboxed inline notation paragraph (content unchanged)
  4. "Case Study: A Patch Escape" -> unboxed "Case study: a patch escape." paragraph; backtick code spans (`hostPath`) converted to proper \texttt{}; diff retained.

**Verification:** Rebuilt with TinyTeX. PDF compiles (14 pages); zero undefined references/citations; references intact through [28] (Ardebili present, no fabricated "Kremer"); per-page geometry scan shows no text past the right margin; overfull-hbox count unchanged at 6 (no new overflow introduced). `paper/access.pdf` updated to this build.

## Change 10 — Overclaiming / precision pass (acted on external reviewer critique)

After integrity, layout, and prose passes, the dominant remaining risk was over-claiming. Addressed all eight "must-fix" items from the reviewer critique. Every number was ground-checked against the released artifacts before editing.

**Must-fix #1 — Metric denominators table.** Added Table~\ref{tab:denominators} (full-width) stating the unit/count/mode/meaning for each headline number (live replay 1,000 manifests; supported 1,264 manifests; supported risk set 1,278 detections; full corpus 15,718 detections / 13,373 patched / 13,338 accepted; Grok-5k 5,000 manifests) plus explicit definitions of "acceptance" (over attempted patches), "auto-fix rate" (over all detections), live "success" (dry-run/apply, zero rollback), and "risk removal".

**Resolved a real internal contradiction (median patch length).** Abstract/full-corpus said "median 9"; RQ4 said "median 5 ops". Verified against artifacts: `unified_eval_summary.json` gives median_patch_ops 8 (supported), 6 (5k), 9 (full corpus); the "5" came from `patch_stats.json` which has only `count: 19`. Rewrote RQ4 to "median 9 operations on the full corpus; 5--8 on the smaller curated slices" so all instances are consistent.

**Must-fix #2 — Qualified every "100% success" claim** (7 sites: abstract, contributions, glance table cell, eval body, baseline comparison, conclusion, "Safety and performance"). "fixed every item" / "100% success" -> "100% dry-run/apply acceptance on a fixture-seeded replay (zero rollbacks)".

**Must-fix #3 — Evidence-status table.** Added Table~\ref{tab:evidence_status} separating Completed (rules pipeline, Grok run, live replay) from replay-based (scheduler), simulated-only (operator A/B, 247 assignments), and planned (human-in-the-loop rotation). Softened the cross-cloud claim: it is reported as replay output across EKS/GKE/AKS-targeted environments, not independently re-verified, with broader generalization marked future work. (Verified `data/cross_cluster/` holds populated 200-manifest results per provider dated 2025-10-24, but the provider environment could not be independently confirmed, so the table states this honestly.)

**Must-fix #4 — Detector-accuracy logic.** Removed the claim that live-cluster success "validates detector performance". Now: the live replay validates remediation *safety* for flagged items, not detector *recall*; recall on uncurated manifests is stated as an open limitation.

**Must-fix #5 — "Safe" -> policy/API-admissible.** Walkthrough and limitations now state the verifier establishes policy/schema/API-admission safety, not full workload semantic equivalence (no guarantee the app starts, passes probes, or tolerates read-only FS / dropped capabilities). Added a hostPath limitation: emptyDir rewrite is policy-safe but not semantically equivalent and should route through human review unless the path is known-disallowed.

**Must-fix #6 — Image-tag selection.** The worked example's `acme/api:1.42.0` is now labeled illustrative; the deterministic fixer requires an operator-configured replacement tag/digest for `no_latest_tag` and otherwise queues the item for human review rather than inventing a version.

**Must-fix #7 — Softened baseline language.** "Polaris never produces a triad-verified fix" -> "is detection-oriented in this setup and does not emit standalone verifier-gated JSON patches". Reframed the Kyverno comparison from out-performing to complementary roles (post-hoc repair of existing manifests + per-patch evidence vs. admission-time mutation).

**Must-fix #8 — Table 2 tiny-count caveat.** Added a sentence noting several per-policy cells rest on small denominators (e.g., no_host_path 1/1, no_privileged 1/3) and are indicative rather than statistically conclusive; the aggregate trend, not individual cells, is the comparison signal.

**Verification:** Rebuilt with TinyTeX. 15 pages; 0 undefined references/citations; refs intact through [28]; overfull-hbox count 6 (the two new tables initially caused a real page-15 margin overflow, fixed by making the evidence-status table full-width `table*`); per-page geometry scan confirms no text past the right margin. `paper/access.pdf` updated.

**Not yet done (reviewer "should-fix" / "nice-to-have", pending your call):** reducing marketing phrasing further; relocating the ~55 inline repo file paths to a reproducibility appendix; adding confidence intervals into the main table; a small human-review study; semantic-breakage analysis. These are improvements, not corrections.
